title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: find the greatest height h at which a vertical elastic column can still carry its own weight, i.e. self-weight buckling (§§25–26). With the horizontal force C set to zero, the deflection equation from §26 is g x + ∫x dy + m y'' = 0, where m = Ebb is the stiffness and g is a constant fixed later by an integral condition.

In §26 Euler noted that in a power series for y the coefficients of x^{3n+2} vanish. The coefficients of x^{3n+1} depend only on α (the initial slope), and those of x^{3n} only on g. On this page (§27) he therefore splits y = αp + gq, which separates the equation into two parts:
(I) ∫x dp + m p'' = 0;
(II) x + ∫x dq + m q'' = 0.

For (I) he takes p = x − A x^4 + B x^7 − C x^10 + D x^13 − ... and matches powers:
- x^2: 1/2 − 12mA = 0, so A = 1/(2·3·4·m).
- x^5: −(4/5)A + 42mB = 0, so B = 4A/(5·6·7·m).
- In general the coefficients are 1·4·7···(3k−2)/((3k+1)! m^k).

For (II) he takes q = −𝔄x^3 + 𝔅x^6 − 𝔄... (alternating) and matches powers:
- x: 1 − 6m𝔄 = 0, so 𝔄 = 1/(2·3·m).
- x^4: −(3/4)𝔄 + 30m𝔅 = 0, so 𝔅 = 3𝔄/(4·5·6·m).
- In general the coefficients are 1·3·6···(3k−3)/((3k)! m^k); these are finished on the next page.

In modern terms, differentiating gives m y''' + x y' + g = 0. So u = y' satisfies the Airy-type equation m u'' + x u = −g. Then p' is the homogeneous solution with u(0)=1, u'(0)=0, a 0F1 hypergeometric series in −x^3/(9m), expressible through Bessel functions of order −1/3 of argument ∝ x^{3/2}. q is a particular solution of the inhomogeneous equation. Both satisfy y''(0) = 0, the moment-free condition at the free end. On the next page, the end condition y(h) = 0 and the definition gh = ∫_0^h y dx produce the transcendental equation h p − p∫q dx + q∫p dx = 0 for the critical height.
errors: Printed ansatz 'p = x − A x^4 + B x^7 + C x^10 + etc.' has the wrong sign on C. The substituted series that follows (−10·9 m C x^8, −(10/11) C x^11) shows the intended form is p = x − A x^4 + B x^7 − C x^10 + D x^13 − ...
The combined equation is printed as 'm α ddp/dx² . m g ddq/dx²'; the '.' should be '+'.
All coefficient recursions on this page check out: A = 1/(24m), B = 4A/(210m), C = 7B/(720m), D = 10C/(1716m), 𝔄 = 1/(6m), 𝔅 = 3𝔄/(120m).

The page does not discuss whether the boundary/end conditions used for the whole problem are physically right. The literature (Truesdell) reports that Euler's 1778 heavy-column treatment was flawed and that the problem was settled correctly only later (Greenhill 1881). Where Euler's slip lies cannot be judged from this page alone.

ideas.what: Splitting the solution into a homogeneous part (multiplied by α) and a particular part (multiplied by g) via the residue classes of exponents mod 3
ideas.modern_name: Superposition of homogeneous and particular solutions; Frobenius/power-series solution of a linear ODE
ideas.where_published: E510 itself and many Euler series-integration papers

ideas.what: Power series with coefficients 1·4·7···/(3k+1)! m^k and 1·3·6···/(3k)! m^k solving m u'' + x u = const
ideas.modern_name: Airy-function series / Bessel functions of order ±1/3 (heavy-column equation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Airy (1838) for the Airy function; Greenhill (1881) for the Bessel-function solution of the heavy column
ideas.where_published: E510 and its companion 1778 column papers; discussed by Truesdell (Opera omnia II.11/2 commentary)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine coefficient determination for Airy-type series in Euler's well-studied (and historically criticized) heavy-column memoir. The link to Airy/Bessel functions is well known from the Greenhill and Truesdell commentary.
transcription_corrections: 'm α . ddp/dx² . m g . ddq/dx²' should read 'm α ddp/dx² + m g ddq/dx²'.
The ansatz as printed reads '+ C x^10'; the intended sign is '− C x^10' (consistent with the substituted series).
